## 🔬 Research Identity

::: intro-block
**Methodological Artificial Intelligence · Urban Data Science · Reproducible Analytical Systems**

Jesús Cáceres-Tello holds a PhD in Data Science from the Complutense University of Madrid, with a research focus on methodological artificial intelligence and urban data science. He combines academic research with extensive experience in public sector digital systems and applied data science.

His work focuses on the evaluation of predictive models under real-world constraints, with emphasis on:

-   Urban environmental modelling and air quality forecasting
-   Machine learning under class imbalance
-   Time series forecasting and temporal validation
-   Hybrid and deep learning architectures
-   Performance–cost trade-off analysis
-   Reproducible research and open science frameworks
-   AI-supported STEM education

His research contributes to the development of transparent, reproducible, and operational AI systems for sustainable urban environments.
:::

## 🎯 Research Mission

::: intro-block
His research aims to develop methodologically robust and reproducible approaches for the evaluation and application of artificial intelligence and data science in complex real-world environments.

This includes:

- Evaluating predictive models under real-world constraints
- Designing reproducible and traceable analytical pipelines
- Analysing performance–cost and robustness trade-offs
- Integrating computational efficiency into model evaluation
- Supporting data-driven decision-making in urban and institutional contexts
- Exploring responsible applications of emerging AI technologies

His research is developed within a broader programme focused on methodological AI, urban data science, and reproducible analytical systems.
:::

## 🏗 Research Infrastructure & Open Science

::: intro-block
All research is developed following open science and reproducibility principles.

All research projects are developed within a structured computational framework:

-   Git-based version control
-   Public repositories with DOI integration (Zenodo)
-   Reproducible scripts and notebooks (R, Python, Quarto)
-   Time-based validation strategies
-   Transparent and standardised performance reporting

Each publication is supported by:

-   An open repository
-   Executable code
-   Structured documentation
-   Publicly accessible data sources

This approach ensures traceability, transparency, and methodological consistency across all research outputs.
:::

## 🎓 Academic Background & Professional Experience

::: intro-block
Jesús Cáceres-Tello holds:

```{=html}
  <ul>
    <li>Ph.D. in Data Science, Faculty of Statistical Studies, Complutense University of Madrid (2026)</li>
  
    <li>Master’s Degree in Artificial Intelligence, IoT and Big Data for Digital Transformation, INESEM Business School (2024)</li>
  
    <li>Master’s Degree in Educational Informatics, University of Alcalá</li>
  
    <li>B.Sc. in Information Systems Engineering, Catholic University of Ávila</li>
  
    <li>Diploma in Computer Science (Business Informatics), University of Málaga</li>
  </ul>
  
<p>His professional experience includes:</p>
  
  <ul>
    <li>Applied data science and artificial intelligence in public-sector environments (Madrid City Council)</li>
    <li>Participation in European and national research projects in health informatics and interoperability</li>
    <li>Development of data-driven systems, predictive models, and business intelligence solutions</li>
    <li>Leadership and coordination of digital infrastructure and analytics initiatives</li>
  </ul>
```

He has been teaching in higher education for over a decade and actively contributes to academic innovation initiatives.
:::
